title: Exceptional rank-one constituents
statement:
Let $\mathcal E$ be either a rank-one constant
Weil sheaf or its tensor product
with an Artin–Schreier sheaf
$\mathcal L_{\psi,ax}$ for some $a\in k_0^\times$. If $\mathcal E$
is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$ on a dense open
$U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$, then the compactly supported
cohomology groups $H_c^i(U,\mathcal E)$ have weights at most $w+i$
for every $i$.

proof.text: Use the finite-field, geometric-Frobenius and adic coefficient conventions of [rem-dl-a1-conventions]. Write $A_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$, $A=A_0\otimes k$, and $j:U_0\hookrightarrow A_0$. Its reduced closed complement $Z_0$ is finite over $k_0$: a proper closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}k_0[x]$ is cut out by a nonzero polynomial $f$, and $k_0[x]/\sqrt{(f)}$ is finite-dimensional over $k_0$. With $f=1$ when the complement is empty, $U_0=D(f)$ is a smooth affine curve. Write the constant rank-one factor as $\mathcal B_b$, $b\in\Qlb^\times$, using [def-wf-constant-weil-twist], and put $L=\Qlb_{A_0}$ in the constant case or $L=\mathcal L_{\psi,ax}$, $a\ne0$, in the other case. Then $\mathcal E_0=\mathcal B_b\otimes L$ restricts to $\mathcal E$. The Artin–Schreier factor is lisse of rank one on the whole line by [lem-fd-as-lisse], so $\mathcal E_0$ is lisse there. Only this restriction identity is needed; no claim about the derived direct image $Rj_*$ is used.

source.place: Opening paragraph: full-line extension and finite complement

proof.text: Set $c=2\log_q|\iota(b)|$. The constant unit is pure of weight zero directly from [def-weil-punctual-weights]; the other possible factor $L$ is pure of weight zero by [lem-fd-as-purity]. Consequently [lem-wf-constant-twist-weight] makes $\mathcal E_0$ pure of weight $c$ at every closed point of $A_0$. This weight equals the given $w$: choose a closed point of $U_0$. Such a point exists explicitly by choosing a finite extension $k'/k_0$ with $\#k'>\deg f$, and an element on which $f$ is nonzero; its image in $D(f)$ is closed. At this point $u$, the rank-one eigenvalue has absolute value both $q_u^{c/2}$ and $q_u^{w/2}$. Since $q_u>1$, $c=w$. Thus purity of weight $w$ holds on the entire line, including the missing points.

source.place: Boundary paragraph: justify the weight at missing points from purity on the nonempty open

proof.text:
Apply field-stage Poincare duality on the smooth separated geometrically connected curve $A_0$, of dimension one. Its structure morphism is smooth separated of finite type, so [cor-pur-smooth-admissibility] supplies the finite-stage constructible admissibility required in the Poincare conventions. Both choices of $L$ are site-perfect: the constant unit is locally free of rank one; for the Artin–Schreier factor this is the lisse rank-one assertion of [lem-fd-as-lisse]. Placed in degree zero, these are bounded complexes of finite projective coefficient modules locally on the site, precisely [def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x]. Thus [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field], at $\Lambda=\Qlb$ and $d=1$, gives finite-dimensional perfect line-valued pairings
$$H_c^i(A,L)\times H^{2-i}(A,L^\vee)\longrightarrow\Qlb(-1).$$
Use these for $i=0,1,2$ below. Properness is not a hypothesis of this duality theorem.

source.place: Step 1: hypotheses and field-stage degreewise duality

proof.text: For $L=\Qlb$, [lem-fd-affine-line-constant-cohomology] identifies $H^0(A,L)$ with the constant sections $\Qlb$ and makes $H^1(A,L)=H^2(A,L)=0$. The pairings in step 3 therefore give $H_c^0(A,L)=H_c^1(A,L)=0$ and $\dim H_c^2(A,L)=1$. The section $1\in H^0(A,L)$ is fixed by the canonical Frobenius. By [cor-pod-untwisted-similitude] the untwisted pairing satisfies $\langle Fx,F1\rangle=q\langle x,1\rangle$. Perfectness makes $x\mapsto\langle x,1\rangle$ an isomorphism of one-dimensional vector spaces, so this equation says that $F$ acts on $H_c^2(A,L)$ by $q$. Thus this Frobenius module is $\Qlb(-1)$.

source.place: Step 1: constant-coefficient calculation and Frobenius normalization

proof.text: For $L=\mathcal L_{\psi,ax}$ with $a\ne0$, [lem-fd-as-lisse] identifies $L^\vee$ with $\mathcal L_{\psi,-ax}$. Here $-a\ne0$ even in characteristic two. The character is the fixed nontrivial prime-field character used in the definition of this sheaf; hence [lem-fd-cohomology-affine-line-character] applies over the algebraically closed geometric field $k$ to the coefficient $-a$. It gives $H^{2-i}(A,L^\vee)=0$ for $i=0,1,2$. The perfect pairings of [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field] force $H_c^i(A,L)=0$ in each of these degrees. No inference about weights or finite-field traces is needed for this vanishing.

Use [lem-wf-constant-twist-cohomology] with the separated finite-type structure morphism $A_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$, the constructible sheaf $L$ in degree zero, and the point twist $\mathcal B_b$. It gives Frobenius-compatible isomorphisms $H_c^i(A,\mathcal E_0)\cong H_c^i(A,L)\otimes\mathcal B_b$. In degrees zero and one these spaces vanish by steps 4–5. In degree two they vanish in the nonconstant-character case, and otherwise form a line with Frobenius eigenvalue $bq$. Step 2 gives $|\iota(bq)|=q^{w/2}q=q^{(w+2)/2}$, so this last line is pure of weight $w+2$ by [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]. In either case the degree-two group has weights at most $w+2$.

source.place: Step 1: constant twisting and the degree-two weight bound

proof.text: Let $i:Z_0\hookrightarrow A_0$ be the reduced closed complement from step 1 and put $B=i^*\mathcal E_0$. Its stalk at a closed point is exactly the same Frobenius representation as that of $\mathcal E_0$ there, so step 2 makes it pure of weight $w$. The finite-boundary lemma [lem-a1-finite-boundary-cohomology], applied to the finite $k_0$-scheme $Z_0$ and this constructible Weil sheaf, gives $H_c^r(Z,B)=0$ for $r\ne0$. The companion statement [lem-a1-finite-boundary-weights] gives weights at most $w$ on $H_c^0(Z,B)$. This also covers $Z_0=\varnothing$.

Apply [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] to $K=\mathcal E_0$ on $A$, with $\Lambda=\Qlb$. All data descend to $k_0$, so this is a Weil-equivariant triangle. Clause 3 of [prop-functor-package], applied to the structure map, identifies its compact-support image with
$$R\Gamma_c(U,\mathcal E)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(A,\mathcal E_0)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(Z,B)\longrightarrow .$$
This uses the package's $\Qlb$ constructible domain, not merely a finite-torsion triangulatedness result. The derived homology long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] is consequently Frobenius-equivariant. Its terms in steps 6–7 give $H_c^0(U,\mathcal E)=0$ from $H_c^{-1}(Z,B)=0$ and $H_c^0(A,\mathcal E_0)=0$, and give
$$H_c^0(Z,B)\twoheadrightarrow H_c^1(U,\mathcal E),\qquad H_c^2(U,\mathcal E)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_c^2(A,\mathcal E_0),$$
since $H_c^1(A,\mathcal E_0)=H_c^1(Z,B)=H_c^2(Z,B)=0$.

source.place: Step 3: localization, compact-support composition, and its long exact sequence

proof.text: By [lem-a1-subquotient-extension-bounds], the Frobenius-stable quotient $H_c^1(U,\mathcal E)$ of $H_c^0(Z,B)$ has weights at most $w$, and hence at most $w+1$ (the same weight filtration works because $w\le w+1$). The degree-two isomorphism of step 8 and step 6 give weights at most $w+2$. Degree zero vanishes. Finally $U_0=D(f)$ is a smooth affine curve and $\mathcal E$ is a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf in degree zero, so [lem-zl-affine-curve-range] gives zero for every degree outside $\{0,1,2\}$. The zero vector space has the empty weight filtration by [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights], for every bound, including the bounds $w+i$ in negative degrees. These assertions prove the required bound for every integer $i$.

source.place: Step 3: subquotient bounds and all remaining degrees
